newsitem.title: USA: Merck acquires Italy's Istituto Gentili.
newsitem.headline: Merck acquires Italy's Istituto Gentili.

text.p: Pharmaceutical company Merck & Co Inc said Tuesday it had bought "substantially all" of the stock of an Italian company in order to strengthen its presence in the country.
"Merck has an option allowing it to acquire the remaining stock of Istituto Gentili over time," it said in a statement.
Merck also said it wanted to secure the intellectual property rights for alendronate, the product that it developed with Istituto Gentili.
It did not elaborate and officials were not immediately available for comment.
The drug, which Merck markets under the trade name Fosamax, is a nonhormonal medicine for the treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
